Subject: Access controls runbook & ops transfer for AtlasOne rollout

Hi Liam / Priya —

Great to connect last week. This thread is to centralize the customer success -> implementation handoff for AtlasOne's SSO + SCIM + IP allowlist integration. Our goal: have a validated runbook and an assigned ops owner before the pilot cutover window on 2026-09-28.

High-level scope:
- SAML SSO (Okta as IdP)
- SCIM provisioning (Okta SCIM API)
- Network restrictions: IP allowlist for SCIM / admin APIs and SAML assertion endpoints
- Service accounts and org policies for provisioning syncs

Immediate asks for your team so we can finalize the runbook:
1) Confirm IdP entityID and SAML metadata XML (or provide metadata URL)
2) Confirm SCIM admin account plan (will AtlasOne create a dedicated SCIM service account in Okta? we need the name/email and whether token rotation is required by your policy)
3) Provide CIDR ranges or static egress IPs that Redwood should whitelist (we support both; static IP preferred)
4) Any org-level policy constraints (minimum NameID format, mandatory attributes for create/update) we should bake into mapping

I'll assign engineering owners for each bullet after we get your answers. Proposed kickoff/ops transfer call: Thu 2026-09-17 10:00 PT — I'll send a calendar invite once we confirm.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Thanks Stephanie —

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Great to connect last week. This thread is to centralize the customer success -> implementation handoff for AtlasOne's SSO + SCIM + IP allowlist integration.

Quick answers from our side:
- IdP: Okta. We can share the metadata XML; I'll attach the metadata file and the ACS/Entity IDs in a follow-up email.
- SCIM: Yes, we'll provision a dedicated SCIM service account in Okta. Priya is owning token creation; we typically rotate tokens every 90 days.
- IPs: Our infra team will try to provide static egress IPs but can also supply a tight CIDR range if needed.
- Org policies: Our HR directory requires email and employeeNumber attributes on create; NameID should be email.

Outstanding question: Does Redwood require SCIM requests to come from a single fixed IP, or do you accept a small CIDR and a signed service account token? If token + CIDR is acceptable, it will be easier for us to avoid a NAT change.

Liam O'Connor
Director, IT Operations
AtlasOne

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlasone.com>, Priya Khatri <priya.k@atlasone.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls runbook & ops transfer for AtlasOne rollout — technical details

Thanks Liam — useful answers. A few technical clarifications from the implementation side so we can lock the runbook: 

1) SCIM endpoints / fields
- Redwood SCIM endpoint (production): https://scim.redwood.ai/v2/AtlasOne
- Required create attributes: userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type eq "work"].value, employeeNumber
- We will supply a mapping template (attached: scim-field-mapping.csv) — please confirm that Okta will push employeeNumber and primary work email.

2) SCIM auth and token rotation
- We support Bearer tokens issued by the customer; token rotation is fine but we need a rotation plan: a minimum 48h overlap window where both old and new tokens are accepted.
- If you rotate every 90 days, provide a scheduled rotation date to avoid sync interruptions.

3) IP allowlist options
- Preferred: one or two static egress IPs from AtlasOne that we whitelist for the SCIM admin API and the SAML metadata fetch (if you host metadata behind protected endpoints).
- Acceptable alternative: a small CIDR (no larger than /28) + token-based auth. If you give us the CIDR, we'll schedule a socket-level verification step during cutover.

4) SAML specifics
- ACS URL we will provide from the runbook template; please confirm NameID format = email, and whether you require encrypted assertions.

5) Rate limits and cutover sequencing
- We will throttle SCIM calls during initial provisioning: ~60 reqs/min. If you have a large directory (>10k users) we should do a staged sync over multiple days.

Action items we need from AtlasOne by EOD Friday (2026-09-17):
- Final IdP metadata XML (or metadata URL)
- SCIM service account email and indication of token rotation cadence
- Preferred IPs or CIDR to whitelist

I'll attach the mapping CSV and a short checklist. If you prefer, we can do a brief run-through in the kickoff call to validate live.
